tool.name: VarDict (C++)
tool.description: calls SNVs and indels from a single BAM (C++ port of VarDict)
tool.command:
ln -s '$select_mode.tumor' ./tumor.bam && ln -s '$select_mode.tumor.metadata.bam_index' ./tumor.bam.bai &&
## INDEX REFERENCE FASTA FILE IF FROM HISTORY #if $reference_source.reference_source_selector == "history": ln -s '$reference_source.ref_file' ./ref.fa && samtools faidx ./ref.fa 2>&1 || echo 'Error running samtools faidx for indexing fasta reference for vardictcpp' >&2 && #else if $reference_source.reference_source_selector == "cached" ln -s '$reference_source.ref_file.fields.path' ./ref.fa && ln -s '${reference_source.ref_file.fields.path}.fai' ./ref.fa.fai && #end if
## Build a whole-chromosome region BED (chr, 1, length, chr). vardictcpp does bounded internal ## chunking (--chunk) with a correct realignment halo, so there is no need to pre-tile the target ## into small overlapping windows: the C++ core keeps memory bounded on large regions itself. #if $interval_file: grep -w -f '$interval_file' ./ref.fa.fai > ./chromosomes.fa.fai && #else ln -s ./ref.fa.fai ./chromosomes.fa.fai && #end if awk 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"} {print \$1, 1, \$2, \$1}' ./chromosomes.fa.fai > ./regions.bed &&
vardictcpp -b "./tumor.bam" -N 'Sample' -G ./ref.fa -z -th \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1} ## Split any region longer than this many bp into internal windows to bound peak memory. --chunk \${VARDICTCPP_CHUNKSIZE:-50000}
-f '$advancedsettings.f' $advancedsettings.k -r '$advancedsettings.r' -B '$advancedsettings.B' -q '$advancedsettings.q' -X '$advancedsettings.X' -P '$advancedsettings.P' -o '$advancedsettings.o' -O '$advancedsettings.O'
## construct VCF table -c 1 -S 2 -E 3 -g 4 ./regions.bed
## postprocessing (scripts from the vardict-java package) | teststrandbias.R | var2vcf_valid.pl -N 'Sample' -E -f '$advancedsettings.f'
> '$all_variants' &&
## Filter for PASS variants awk 'BEGIN {FS=OFS="\t"} substr(\$0, 1, 1) == "#" {print \$0; next} \$7 == "PASS" {print \$0}' '$all_variants' > '$passed_variants'

param.label: Perform local realignment
param.help: Local realignment rescues long indels from soft-clipped reads. Uncheck to disable.

param.label: Minimum number of reads supporting the variant
Minimum number of reads for determining strand bias
Maximum average read position for a variant to be considered.
Maximum number of extended bases after indel to look for mismatches
Minimum phred score for a base to be considered a good call
Minimum quality ratio [(good_quality_reads)/(bad_quality_reads+0.5)] (based on definition of a good call; see previous option)

tool.help:
VarDict (C++) =============
**vardictcpp** is a C++ port of the VarDict variant caller. On single-sample calling it reproduces the variants of the Java implementation (VarDictJava) while using a fraction of the memory and running faster, because it holds native per-position counters instead of the JVM object graph and needs no Java heap.
This wrapper runs single-sample SNV and indel calling and converts the result to VCF with VarDict's own ``teststrandbias.R`` and ``var2vcf_valid.pl`` post-processing scripts, so the output columns match the regular VarDict tool.
Memory and large regions -------------------------
VarDict's memory scales with how large a single work unit (region) is: one big region is processed on one thread and holds that whole span's tables at once. vardictcpp splits any region longer than ``VARDICTCPP_CHUNKSIZE`` bp (default ``50000``) into internal windows with a correct realignment halo, so peak memory stays bounded even on whole-chromosome targets while the emitted calls are unchanged. Lower the value further for extremely deep data or when calling at ``-f 0``.
Scope -----
Only **single-sample** mode is wrapped here. Paired/somatic and amplicon calling exist in the C++ port but are not yet exposed by this wrapper; use the Java VarDict tool for those modes.
For more information see the VarDict documentation_.
.. _documentation: https://github.com/AstraZeneca-NGS/VarDictJava
